statements.status_notes: Open question: whether libglvnd will validate the server-supplied attribute count, or rule on the dispute. CVE-2023-45924 (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2023-45924) is a crash in libGLX: __glXGetDrawableScreen() in src/GLX/libglxproto.c takes numAttribs from the X server's GLXGetDrawableAttributes reply and walks the returned attribute list without checking it against the reply length, so a malicious X server can make the client read past the buffer. The CVE record cites libglvnd issue https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/glvnd/libglvnd/-/issues/242 and the proposed fix https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/glvnd/libglvnd/-/merge_requests/295, and is tagged disputed because there are no common situations in which users need uninterrupted operation against an attacker-controlled X server. libglvnd has not ruled on it: the issue and the merge request are both still open. Both builds of this owner in the DHI Debian repository are rebuilds of Debian's libglvnd 1.7.0-1 with no patches added; Debian's patch series for 1.7.0-1 is empty, and we checked that __glXGetDrawableScreen() in the 1.7.0 source still loops over rep.numAttribs without a length check. Debian lists the CVE as unfixed in trixie and rates it unimportant: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2023-45924
